texts.li: {A_nameDef} wrinkled {A_possessive} nose at the smell from the {THING} across the room.
The {THING} in the corner still smelled of the last carcass, and {A_nameDef} could think of nothing else.
{A_nameDef} looked at the stains on the {THING} and wished someone would move it somewhere else.
[eating] {A_nameDef} ate quickly, with the smell of the {THING} at {A_possessive} back.
[eating] {A_nameDef} pushed the plate away half full. Hard to enjoy a meal next to the {THING}.
[!eating] {A_nameDef} lay down to the smell of old blood from the {THING} in the room.
[morning,!eating] {A_nameDef} woke up to the smell of the {THING} again.
[child] "Why do we sleep next to where the animals get cut up?" {A_nameDef} asked.
[eating] {A_nameDef} chewed slowly and tried not to look at the {THING}.
[eating] The {THING} was too close to the table for {A_nameDef}'s liking, and the meal tasted of it.
[!eating] {A_nameDef} pulled the blanket up over {A_possessive} nose against the smell of the {THING}.
[!eating] The smell of the {THING} seemed worse in the dark, and {A_nameDef} lay awake with it.
[eating] {A_nameDef} left half the bowl, with the {THING} so close.
{A_nameDef} asked aloud who had thought it a good idea to put the {THING} in here.
Every time someone used the {THING} by {A_nameDef}'s bed, the cold came straight in.
{A_nameDef} stuffed a rolled-up shirt along the bottom of the {THING}. The draught came in anyway.
[morning] {A_nameDef} had felt the cold air from the {THING} across the bed all night.
[morning] {A_nameDef} woke up with cold feet. The draught from the {THING} again.
[evening] {A_nameDef} pulled the blanket up and turned away from the cold coming in at the {THING}.
[morning,snow] Snow had blown in under the {THING} by {A_nameDef}'s bed during the night.
[child,morning] {A_nameDef} had slept with {A_possessive} head under the blanket because of the cold from the {THING}.
[morning] The first thing {A_nameDef} felt on waking was the cold off the {THING}.
[morning] {A_nameDef} got up stiff and chilled, with the wind still pushing at the {THING} beside the bed.
[morning] {A_nameDef}'s joints ached from a night next to the cold {THING}.
[morning] There was frost on the inside of the {THING} by {A_nameDef}'s bed.
[evening] {A_nameDef} lay listening to the wind work at the {THING} by the bed.
[evening] {A_nameDef} went to bed in two layers, for the draught from the {THING}.
[child,morning] {A_nameDef} asked for another blanket, because the {THING} had let the cold in all night.
{A_nameDef} slept at the far end of the bed, as far from the {THING} as {A_pronoun} could get.
{A_nameDef} could feel the cold from the {THING} right through the blanket.
The {THING} by {A_nameDef}'s bed let in a thin, steady cold, and {A_nameDef} slept badly for it.
